thread:
rachel: Seeing a strange parse error in the Python SDK during auth refresh. Sample app hits a timeout and the SSE parser raises a JSONDecodeError because a partial delimiter '\n\n' arrives split across reconnects.

pablo: which sdk version and which transport?

rachel: py-sdk v0.9.1, using requests-eventsource shim. Repro: trigger an auth refresh mid-stream (short TTL token). The client gets fragment A, then auth refresh, then fragment B where the separator boundary between events is split: part of the separator comes before refresh and the rest after reconnect. The parser thinks it's part of payload.

emma: can you paste the raw bytes?

rachel: logs: 
```
[net] recv 0x1a: `data: {"role":"assistant","content":"Hello`
[auth] token expired -> refreshing
[net] connection closed (401)
[auth] new token acquired
[net] reconnect
[net] recv 0x2b: `\n"}`
```
So the boundary `\n\n` that normally separates SSE events got split and the parser concatenates leading `\n` to the payload tail, producing `"Hello\n` which eventually leads to malformed JSON when the closing brace comes separated.

chad: hmm, our parser expects each SSE 'data:' block includes a complete JSON payload and splits on the double newline. If the double newline is split across connection boundaries, the stream reassembly must consider that. Are we storing trailing incomplete delimiter fragments anywhere?

rachel: requests-eventsource currently appends incoming chunks to a buffer and scans for `\n\n`. When reconnecting we naively prepend the new data to the buffer, but if the buffer ended with a single `\n` and new data starts with `\"}` we miss the fact that a delimiter existed across the boundary.

pablo: seems like two fixes: 1) normalize reassembly to treat any single trailing `\n` as potentially part of the delimiter and don't attempt to parse until either another `\n` arrives or a timeout, 2) stamp fragments with event offsets/seq so we can re-run boundary detection post-reconnect. Second helps for cross-sdk parity.

emma: we should be careful about waiting too long; holding a fragment waiting for a possible `\n` could add noticeable latency. Maybe use a tiny grace window (e.g., 50ms) before forcing parse, configurable. Also add an edge-case test in unit suite that simulates split-delimiter across reconnect.

chad: server-side could also help: send explicit event-id or include a small terminator token that is less likely to be split. But we can't rely on server changes for SDK parity. Client-side reassembly is the fix.

rachel: I'll try fix 1 first: treat trailing `\n` as incomplete delimiter and wait up to 40ms for additional input before parsing; if none arrives, proceed but log a warning. Also add a defensive fallback to attempt to repair JSON by looking for the first `{` before parsing to avoid `JSONDecodeError` crashing user code.

pablo: please also add an integration test in `tests/stream_reconnect.py` that runs the sample app with a token TTL of 200ms and forces reconnects to see the split-delimiter case. Tag it slow and run in CI optional matrix.

emma: small note: update the docs for py-sdk streaming reliability and mention the config knobs `delimiter_grace_ms` and `reassembly_debug` so support can enable them when debugging.

infra-bot: Reminder: any changes to `requests-eventsource` adapter must run `tox -e py39` and the streaming regression suite in the infra pipeline.

rachel: will open a tiny PR with the grace-window + unit/integration test, mark WIP. Thanks y'all :pray:
